name: Zerubbabel
role: Governor of Judah who rebuilt the temple
whenBasis: The first return under Cyrus (≈538 BC) to the temple's completion in the sixth year of Darius I (Ezra 6:15), ≈515 BC; Haggai 1:1 dates him as governor in Darius's second year, ≈520 BC.
summary: Son of Shealtiel and grandson of King Jehoiachin, who led the first exiles home from Babylon with the high priest Jeshua. They rebuilt the altar and laid the temple's foundation, then refused the help of the people of the land, who stopped the work. In the second year of Darius, stirred by Haggai and Zechariah, Zerubbabel and Jeshua began again, and the temple was finished. Haggai called him the LORD's signet ring.
body: As the foundation is laid, the old men who had seen the first temple weep aloud while others shout for joy. Zechariah's word to him is “Not by might nor by power, but by My Spirit”: his hands laid the foundation, and his hands will complete it.

Chronicles lists him as a son of Pedaiah, Shealtiel's brother; everywhere else he is son of Shealtiel. He stands in both Matthew's and Luke's genealogies of Jesus. Haggai's signet ring takes up the image of Jeremiah's word to his grandfather Coniah (Jehoiachin), that the LORD would pull him off even if he were His signet ring.

later.text: Sheshbazzar, the prince of Judah to whom Cyrus gave the vessels, is said to have laid the temple's foundation, as Zerubbabel is. Ibn Ezra takes Sheshbazzar to be Zerubbabel's name in the Chaldean tongue, and C. F. Keil holds it beyond doubt, comparing Ezra 5:16 with 3:8; Keil names Schrader and Nöldeke as objecting. Rashi gives the rabbis' view that Sheshbazzar is Daniel.

sources.title: Ibn Ezra on Ezra 1:8
sources.note: Hebrew: 'לששבצר - הוא זרובבל ונקרא כן בלשון כשדים' (rendered here: to Sheshbazzar: he is Zerubbabel, and is so called in the Chaldean tongue)

sources.title: Rashi on Ezra 1:8
sources.note: tr. A. J. Rosenberg: 'Our Rabbis said: “Sheshbazzar is identical with Daniel, and why was he called Sheshbazzar? Because he endured six troubles”'

sources.title: Biblical Commentary on the Old Testament: Ezra, Nehemiah and Esther, on Ezra 1:8
sources.author: C. F. Keil (Keil and Delitzsch)
sources.note: 'The identity of Sheshbazzar with Zerubbabel, which has been objected to by Schrader and Nöldeke, is placed beyond a doubt by a comparison of Ezra 5:16 with Ezra 3:8'

traditions: the same man: Ibn Ezra; C. F. Keil; Theographic's data
